title: JavaScript Array Methods Check
description: Test your ability to choose and predict common array methods like forEach, map, filter, reduce, find, some, every, includes, and entries.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which method is best when you want to transform every item and get a new array of the same length?
questions.explanation: `map` transforms each element and returns a new array with the same length.

questions.prompt:
What does this code return?
```js
const result = [1, 2, 3].forEach((number) => number * 2);
```
questions.explanation: `forEach` always returns `undefined`; it is meant for side effects.
With braces, the arrow callback needs an explicit `return`. Without it, each result is `undefined`.

questions.prompt: Which method is best when you want all items that match a condition?
questions.explanation: `filter` returns a new array containing all matching items.

questions.prompt:
What does this code return?
```js
const result = [1, 2, 3, 4].filter((number) => number > 2);
```
questions.explanation: `filter` keeps all items where the condition is true.

questions.prompt: Which method is best when you want the first matching item itself?
questions.explanation: `find` returns the first matching element, or `undefined` if no match exists.

questions.prompt:
What does this code return?
```js
const result = [5, 8, 12, 20].find((number) => number > 10);
```
questions.explanation: `find` stops at the first matching item, which is `12`.

questions.prompt: Which method is best for answering: "Does at least one item match?"
questions.explanation: `some` returns `true` when at least one item passes the condition.

questions.prompt:
What does this code return?
```js
const result = [2, 4, 6].every((number) => number % 2 === 0);
```
questions.explanation: Every number in the array is even, so `every` returns `true`.

questions.prompt: Which method is best when you want to turn an array into one accumulated result?
questions.explanation: `reduce` builds one final accumulated result, such as a number, object, string, or array.

questions.prompt:
What does this code return?
```js
const result = [1, 2, 3].reduce((sum, number) => sum + number, 0);
```
questions.explanation: The accumulator starts at `0` and adds each number, producing `6`.
`includes` checks whether the array contains the exact value and returns a boolean.

questions.prompt: Which method gives index-value pairs like `[0, "Apple"]`?
questions.explanation: `entries()` returns an iterator of `[index, value]` pairs.

questions.prompt:
What does this code return?
```js
const result = [[1, 2], [3, 4]].flat();
```

questions.explanation: `flatMap` maps each item, then flattens the result one level.
